name: spec-driven-development
description: Spec-driven development workflow: steering documents, feature specs (requirements/design/tasks/review-log), verification, and agent-based implementation on a generator/arbiter split — the main agent arbitrates while persistent subagent sessions author, implement (parallel groups by file-disjointness), test, and review to 0 issues. Tests are specified as spec-anchored cases in design.md and written by a dedicated agent kept blind to the implementation, so the suite survives refactoring instead of rotting. Enforces 'no spec, no code' discipline, with a ticket registry (one question per ticket, records never deleted) and a roadmap tree that holds only structure and references tickets by id - both JSON, driven by one validating script - and an advisor gate that settles clear-cut decisions instead of interrupting the user. Executor sessions are bounded by two checkpoints that inject rather than cut: one inside the executor has it send the arbiter a status every N tool calls while it keeps working - so drift is visible mid-dispatch and a correction reaches the executor where it stands, with nothing stopped or discarded, and one at resume that retires a session at 400K — far below the point the harness would autocompact it, so an executor never ends up working from a summary of its own design basis.
